A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, theoretical setting and three principal theorems. The complete texts, equations, references and v2's added simulation appendix are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 contains theoretical results, proofs and references, but no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: Appendix A reports two original simulation studies, with empirical deviation curves in Figure 2 and estimator comparisons in Figure 3.

M1.justification: The empirical mean itself is unchanged. V2 adds an auxiliary cutoff estimator in Section 3.4: estimate coordinates through k(n)=Theta(n) empirically and set the remainder to 1/2. Section 3.3 also corrects the displayed pooling sum from repeated p-hat_n(j) to p-hat_n(i).

E1.justification: V1 has no empirical evaluation coverage. V2 introduces a q-controlled deviation study and simulations labelled uniform, triangular, Beta(2,2), exponential, 1/n-scaled and Gaussian in Appendix A, establishing substantial new synthetic evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix A.2 and Figure 3 introduce the paper's first empirical comparison, evaluating EME against simple averaging. Although these estimator ideas appeared theoretically in v1, no corresponding empirical comparator set was evaluated there.

E3.justification: V2 introduces two simulation protocols rather than revising existing experiments. Figure 2 evaluates average supremum deviation across six q values and sample sizes from 10 to 1000; Figure 3 compares estimator errors over sample sizes from 10 to 10000 across six distribution scenarios.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds checks of theoretical decay and lower-bound tightness across q values, plus analyses of how averaging advantages vary with distribution and k. These sensitivity and theory-validation analyses have no empirical counterpart in v1.

E5.justification: V2 first reports averaging over J=100, 1000 and 10000 repetitions in Appendix A.1 and trial counts k=10, 50, 100 and 500 in A.2. This adds repetition information, but neither confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests nor seeds are supplied.

E6.justification: V2 adds all empirical results. Figure 2 shows deviations decreasing with sample size alongside theoretical curves. Figure 3 shows averaging errors below EME errors across the six displayed distributions, with larger k reducing averaging error. These are newly reported outcomes, not improvements over v1 experimental scores.

T1.justification: New Proposition 1 and Section 3.4 prove learnability of Q={p: |p_j-1/2|<=c/sqrt(j)}, a strongly symmetric, nondecaying family establishing the necessity of Theorem 1's decay assumption. V2 also corrects proof formulas, including the inclusion-exclusion initialization from alpha_1(x)=1 to alpha_1(x)=x. The three original theorem statements remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution summary retain the same three headline claims: maximal learnability under restrictions, minimax risk bounds, and learnable extensions when restrictions are relaxed. EME names the same explicitly defined sample mean previously called MLE; the added proposition refines the assumptions.

C2.justification: V2 distinguishes EME from likelihood maximization over restricted families, adds the conclusion that decay is necessary, and interprets simulations as supporting tightness and averaging advantages. However, the new necessity conclusion conflicts with the retained open-problems paragraph saying decay is probably unnecessary.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds limited reproducibility information through explicit simulation parameter grids and distribution specifications such as Beta(2,2). It supplies no code access, software, hardware or complete data-generation and error-computation instructions.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work positioning are retained. Expanded publication details for references such as Catoni and Hopkins are bibliographic updates, not additions to the research literature being compared.

P1.justification: V2 expands the title, replaces MLE with EME throughout much of the paper, adds a terminology explanation and makes localized prose corrections. The existing narrative and section order largely remain; the new proposition and appendix extend rather than extensively rewrite them.

P2.justification: V1 has no figures or tables. V2 adds a step-profile illustration in Figure 1 and two full-page, six-panel simulation figures. Numerous existing equations are also reformatted into multiline displays, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 corrects the pooling formula and inclusion-exclusion base case, clarifies EME versus MLE, and adds a useful constructive result establishing decay's necessity. These improve mathematical precision. The contradictory retained open-problems paragraph and missing simulation generation/error definitions limit the overall gain; the added plots alone do not establish stronger validation.
